findings.claim: Deleting .github/workflows/knowledge.yml leaves the user-facing how-to pointing at a file that no longer exists. docs/how-to/install-the-plugin-and-the-ci-action.md says its workflow examples are "quoted from" the shipped .github/workflows/knowledge.yml (line 25), and step 4 (line 178-179) tells readers that the workflow to create "is the shipped .github/workflows/knowledge.yml" with uses: ./ swapped for a ref. The plan's scope covers only ci.yml and tests/test_ci.py, so the change would ship a docs page whose source claim is false, in a repository whose whole job is keeping docs current. The plan must name the docs change in scope: either re-point the how-to at ci.yml's knowledge job (which uses SHA-pinned actions unlike the quoted block) or keep a standalone example workflow the doc can quote.
The how-to doc quoted the shipped knowledge.yml, which the plan deletes, without the plan updating the doc.

Step 4 of the how-to says the quoted workflow is ci.yml's knowledge job with actions/checkout 'at its version tag instead of a commit SHA'. ci.yml pins checkout at v7.0.1, but the quoted block uses actions/checkout@v4, so a reader takes v4 to be the tag of the shipped pin, which is false. Say what the block actually uses (for example 'actions/checkout@v4 instead of the pinned commit SHA'), and keep the block's content unchanged as the plan asks.
